profile.name: Vijay Kumar
profile.headline: I build software that gets closer to the system.
profile.summary: From Linux network diagnostics to concurrent C++ systems and AI-enabled applications, I turn complex technical ideas into practical, testable software.
profile.about: I’m an M.Tech CSE student specializing in Cybersecurity at Delhi Technological University, with MCA and BCA foundations from IGNOU. I enjoy building software where reliability, debugging, and security matter—from backend APIs and automated network checks to system-level experiments. I’m interested in software engineering, SDET and automation, networking, and security engineering roles where I can ship useful tools, test carefully, and keep learning.
profile.availability: Open to software engineering, SDET / automation, networking, and cybersecurity opportunities.

projects.title: WiFiTestLab
projects.description: A Linux-first, modular Python/Pytest framework for validating Wi-Fi interface state, association, IP configuration, gateway reachability, DNS, and Internet access. Captures diagnostic evidence with tcpdump/tshark and summarizes latency, packet loss, and DNS response time.
projects.details: Designed around repeatable checks and useful failure evidence rather than a one-off connectivity test. The goal is to make Wi-Fi troubleshooting easier to reproduce, compare, and discuss in an SDET or network engineering review.

projects.title: MiniDB — Thread-Safe In-Memory Database
projects.description: A C++17 project exploring a thread-safe in-memory key-value store, skip-list-based data organization, transaction boundaries, and write-ahead logging (WAL) concepts.
projects.details: A systems-oriented project for discussing concurrency, ACID properties, transaction lifecycle, and how a write-ahead log can support recovery-oriented design. Keep the repository link updated so reviewers can inspect the implementation directly.

projects.title: CacheSim — Direct-Mapped Cache Simulator
projects.description: A configurable C++17 simulator that maps memory addresses into tag, index, and block-offset fields and tracks cache hits, misses, and hit rate across access patterns.
projects.details: Built to make memory hierarchy behavior concrete: vary cache capacity and block size, follow address mapping, and observe how locality changes the hit/miss profile.
